paragraphs.source_en: As the convoy passed through Armenian villages, Captanian saw houses with broken windows and open doors, the furniture scattered outside, and a church treated likewise, its Bibles torn to shreds and ritual objects thrown on the floor.” When the convoy reached the village of Tonuz (today Sarkisla), five hours from Sivas, the men, including her husband, were separated from the rest of the caravan and forced into a stable.*° The women screamed at the gendarmes to release their men. Despite the women’s cries of despair, the soldiers forced them to continue their journey without the men.

Over the following days the remaining refugees rested in Kirkg6z along with thousands of other Armenian deportees from every social class. In the whole area there was only one well, near which many ill and dying people lay. Corpses began to putrefy, ‘which befouled the air and poisoned the living.** The next morning the journey continued on foot. The first thing Captanian saw was a wagon full of children, rounded up by the municipality of Malatya. Thousands of orphans were gathered in the city, without care, emaciated.*° They died like flies.”
